title: Mutation responses carry the post-mutation work state
description: Context: a 2h47m dabble-employee-app agent session made 300 CLI calls with 24 failures. Failure clusters: 117 read-only work show polls (~40% of all calls), 14 identical failed sync refresh retries, 6 vault init retries, 66 agent finish calls with only 2 standalone evidence records, 6 NOT_FOUND finish/release (ownership confusion), 1 CONFLICT claim, 2 POLICY_VIOLATION sprint closes. Design principle for this mission: every response (success or error) must carry enough state that the correct next action is derivable without another read, and the honest path (evidence, ownership, health) must be the path of least resistance. Problem: agents call work show after nearly every mutation (117 polls in the audited session) because mutating commands do not return the resulting state. Change: every mutating work/agent lifecycle command (work claim, work reserve, work release, work renew, work close, work reopen, agent start, agent finish) must include in its --json data payload the same work-item view that work show would return immediately after the mutation, including status, reservation state, gates, and open blockers. Where: apps/cli/src/commands.ts handlers and the shared response composer in packages/engine/src/runtime.ts; mirror in apps/mcp/src/tools.ts so MCP callers get the same shape. Constraint: additive only, do not rename existing payload fields; existing tests in tests/runtime/cli.test.ts and mcp.test.ts must keep passing with additions asserted.
acceptanceCriteria: work claim/release/renew/close/reopen and agent start/finish --json payloads each embed the post-mutation work-show view
MCP tool responses expose the same embedded state
tests/runtime/cli.test.ts asserts the embedded state for at least claim, finish, and close
